newsitem.title: DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF CONGO: Kabila troops arrest Tshisekedi at his home.
newsitem.headline: Kabila troops arrest Tshisekedi at his home.

text.p: Soldiers from President Laurent Kabila's army arrested veteran opposition leader Etienne Tshisekedi on Thursday, hours after he addressed a student gathering, witnesses said.
"They broke into his bedroom and picked him up," one witness told Reuters after the soldiers took Tshisekedi from his home after nightfall on Thursday.

Kabila, who toppled veteran dictator Mobutu Sese Seko after a seven-month civil war in May, has banned all political activity and all political parties, with the exception of his own Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo.
"They say they have been given the order to take him away. They are armed to the teeth," Tshisekedi's adviser, Marcel Mbayo, said of the soldiers earlier.
The soldiers spent several house at the house. It was not immediately clear where they took Tshisekedi or why.

Tshisekedi told a crowd of thousands of students at Kinshasa University that he was in touch with Kabila's Alliance to "harmonise conflicting views" on the institutions of the Democratic Republic of the Congo.

Tshisekedi was the most popular domestic opponent of Mobutu and still enjoys a strong following in Kinshasa. His supporters have marched in defiance of the government ban. Soldiers broke up some marches by firing in the air, others they let go ahead.
Tshisekedi said talks had begun last month, a week after Kabila took power in the former Zaire.
"You will be pleased with the outcome of this dialogue. It will match the expectations of the people of this country. An eight-member commission has been set up," he said to cheers.

Tshisekedi did not elaborate on the items under discussion but suggested that the contacts would lead to the formation of a new government and that he could soon meet Kabila for the first time since he declared himself president.
"It will be a question of a transitional government to organise elections. This government will also solve the problem (of nationality) in eastern Congo," Tshisekedi said.
Ethnic strife has claimed thousands of lives in Kivu, in the east. It is not clear who is "Congolese" and who is not in these provinces bordering Rwanda and Burundi.
Kabila's Alliance dominates the current government. His Rwandan-backed rebellion began in Kivu in October.
Many of his Tutsi-dominated forces initially took up arms to claim the Zairean citizenship which Mobutu denied them.

"We have thanked our foreign friends who have helped us to get rid of the dictator in the final stage of our fight. But this objective has been achieved, now they (foreign friends) have to leave," Tshisekedi said, without further details.
Many Congolese say Rwandan, Ugandan and Burundian soldiers are in the ranks of the Alliance forces. The government has denied suggestions of a foreign presence in the new army.
